prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Make an art-direction revision of the supplied Tequila Kill gameplay image: add lived-in interiors, modest breakable props, and genuinely distinct overhead character silhouettes.
Input image 1 is the edit target; images 2 and 3 are historical PORTRAIT identity references for Poncho and Garcia, not gameplay camera references.

PRESERVE THE ACCEPTED LOOK: same 16:9 composition, same perfectly vertical 90-degree bird's-eye 2D orthographic view, same two open-roof rooms, paths and doorway positions, same restrained pixel art scale imagined at 640x360 with 32px tiles. Same straw-yellow quiet sand, cool blue-gray stones, ochre outcrops, burgundy couch, warm wood, shadows falling down-left. No three-quarter view, no visible faces or fronts of bodies, no 3D makeover, no cartoon illustration. Four small fighters remain in the same places. Preserve broad clear movement lanes and the readable center.

LIVED-IN INTERIORS: the large left room is a worn saloon. Keep the counter and couch. Add 2–3 plain ceramic mugs and a serving tray on the bar, a folded cloth, a small ceramic water jug, a short shelf seen as an overhead plank with small crockery shapes, a restrained faded woven rug by the couch, a poker hand and small chips on the existing central table. A second small table with two wooden stools fits along a side wall; a coat and broad hat hang in a small rack footprint near the entrance. Leave at least half of the room's floor open. The smaller right room is a simple inhabited back room: keep its table; add a small bedroll with pillow along the lower wall, a storage chest, two sacks of grain and a tiny cooking shelf with an iron pot against the upper wall. Household objects are recognizable but tiny and subordinate to the fighters. No extra people, pets or crowds. NO additional glass bottles: exactly ONE tequila bottle in the entire scene, carried by the central player. Ceramic cups, bowls and squat clay jugs are fine.

LIMITED DESTRUCTION VISUAL CUES: most props are intact. Show one exterior wooden crate with a broken cross-plank and a few compact splinters, one indoor wooden chair with a snapped backrest and a few slats directly beside it, and one chipped terracotta pot by an interior wall. Damage localized to these lightweight props; keep building walls, floors and main room furniture intact. No ruined buildings or debris carpet, no explosions or fire. This is an exploratory depiction of limited breakability, not a finalized destruction system.

CHARACTER IDENTITY MUST CHANGE, independently of player marker color:
- Central green-marked carrier is PONCHO: large pale straw circular sombrero with olive-green tall crown, dark brown poncho peeking out around the lower half as a small triangular fringed edge. Same faithful overhead hat-led design, only shoulders/cloth edges peek out. Green bottle beside him, broken cream objective ring retained.
- Right red-marked shooter is GARCIA: visibly smaller dark charcoal wide-brim military hat with a small cream insignia, blue-violet squared shoulder corners and red neckerchief triangle peeking out from beneath the hat. Black hat + square blue shoulders must make a distinctly different silhouette from Poncho. Refer to his original portrait for colors. Do not show his face.
- Blue-marked player leaving the saloon is an UNNAMED SILHOUETTE STUDY A, not an established roster character: a narrow weathered brown oval cowboy hat with one clearly upturned brim edge and a short blue scarf tail behind it. Smaller, asymmetric outline; no face.
- Ochre-marked lower-right player is an UNNAMED SILHOUETTE STUDY B: an extra-wide low cream sombrero with visibly angular clipped brim ends, dark flat crown, mustard cloth edge. Broad horizontal silhouette distinct from Poncho's round shape. No face.
Keep each fighter within roughly the same 32–48 source-pixel footprint. Weapons remain small gun shapes; do not invent new weapons or abilities. Retain the four colored ground markers for PLAYER identity, while hat/cloth geometry communicates CHARACTER identity. Keep the tiny shot, compact muzzle flash and two small dash dust puffs. No HUD or labels on the scene. No text, logos or watermark. Color alone must not be the only character distinction.
